text:
ashley-support: FYI customer FjordAnalytics reporting sudden TLS failures after our cert rotation at ~03:12 UTC. App servers in their VPC started getting javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException for some JVM clients, others OK. ticket: #INC-9021
jon-ops: Can you paste the exact error and a curl/openssl repro? java stacktraces are usually informative here.
ashley-support: Customer sent this Java stack (abbreviated):
```
javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: General SSLEngine problem
Caused by: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException: unable to find valid certification path to requested target
    at sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilder.build(SunCertPathBuilder.java:141)
    ...
```
They also tried `curl -v https://api.private.fjord.local` from a bastion and got:
```
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (4):
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate:
*  subject: CN=api.private.fjord.local
*  start date: Feb 19 03:12:11 2026 GMT
*  expire date: May 19 03:12:11 2026 GMT
*  issuer: CN=Fjord Intermediate CA
*  SSL: certificate subject name (api.private.fjord.local) matched
*  SSL: certificate verify ok.
> GET /health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.private.fjord.local\n< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
So curl doesn't show a verify error, but Java clients fail.
kevin-eng: Interesting — suggests a cert path building difference between OpenSSL and the JVM. Can you grab the full chain dump from the server? `echo | openssl s_client -connect api.private.fjord.local:443 -showcerts` and `openssl x509 -noout -text` on each cert.
maria-sre: Pasted server chain dump from their bastion: (trimmed)
```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.private.fjord.local
   i:/CN=Fjord Intermediate CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIB... (leaf)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIC... (intermediate)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIE... (root)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
Opened the intermediate with `openssl x509 -in intermediate.pem -noout -text` and saw: Basic Constraints: CA:FALSE
kevin-eng: CA:FALSE for the intermediate. That would let OpenSSL still build a path in many cases (it uses the provided chain) but the JVM's cert path builder validates BasicConstraints strictly for CA certificates and will refuse to treat that intermediate as a CA. That matches the SunCertPathBuilderException.
ashley-support: Oh wow. How did that intermediate end up with CA:FALSE? Rotation ran and rotator uploaded the bundle we generated from our onboarding script. rotation-bot reported successful upload at 1768002730.
rotation-bot: rotator: uploaded cert bundle for tenant fjord-123 at 2026-02-20T03:12:10Z (upload_id: rtr-8843)
jon-ops: Could be an accidental mixup where a signing cert was picked instead of the CA cert, or the intermediate got regenerated with wrong constraints. We need to confirm the intermediate's cert fields. Can someone check the issuer cert serial and compare to our catalog?
maria-sre: I compared the intermediate serial and CN to our model onboarding list — it looks like the uploaded intermediate is actually the intermediate signing cert (int-signer) rather than the CA-signed intermediate (int-ca). The int-signer has BasicConstraints: CA:FALSE since it's an end-entity used for cross-signing.
kevin-eng: That explains it. OpenSSL will accept the chain since the server presented the chain and the leaf verifies up to a root, but the JVM's PKIX builder refuses to treat int-signer as a CA. Two remediation routes: 1) re-upload correct intermediate (int-ca with CA:TRUE) and prompt customer to restart JVMs if they cache the trust path, or 2) temporarily enable a compatibility fallback on their side (not ideal). We should prioritize re-upload + rollback plan.
ashley-support: Customer impact: high (auth errors on production JVM workloads). They've started a partial rollback to the previous bundle but want us to fix the canonical chain.
jon-ops: Agreed. kevin, can you prepare a corrected bundle? Include only leaf -> int-ca (CA:TRUE) -> root. Also validate `openssl verify -CAfile root.pem -untrusted int-ca.pem leaf.pem` and test against a java client: `JSSE` will accept if intermediate has CA:TRUE.
kevin-eng: On it. I have a candidate int-ca.pem from our catalog. I'll assemble bundle, run verification and then push to rotator with a replacement upload_id=rtr-8843-fix. Plan: 1) prepare bundle and test on our staging JVM (openjdk11), 2) coordinate with jon for safe upload window, 3) notify customer and push.
maria-sre: Monitoring: TLS handshake failures spiked to 18% for that tenant between 03:12 and 03:26 UTC, request retries masked some client errors so overall 502s grew. I'll keep the incident dashboard open.
rotation-bot: rotator: uploaded replacement bundle (upload_id: rtr-8843-fix) at 2026-02-20T03:42:15Z
jon-ops: After replacement, customer reports Java clients are back to normal on preliminary checks. ashley, confirm with customer and close escalation if green.
ashley-support: Confirmed with FjordAnalytics — JVMs show normal behavior post-replace and retries cleared queues. They're keeping the rollback in progress until EOD but say impact is resolved. Marking incident HIGH -> mitigated. Ticket updated #INC-9021.
kevin-eng: Follow-up action items: add a pre-upload validation to rotator that checks BasicConstraints for any intermediate certs (must be CA:TRUE) and a small integration test that runs a Java PKIX path build against the bundle before marking success. I'll open a PR.
maria-sre: Also adding a short-run alert rule to detect sudden JVM-specific SunCertPathBuilderException spikes per tenant.
ashley-support: Thanks team. Customer happy for now. Closing slack thread but keeping ticket until postmortem done. :white_check_mark:
